steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Facts: Nigeria is located in West Africa with a population of over 220 million (2023), making it Africa's most populous country. Its GNI per head is approximately $2,160 (2022), classifying it as an NEE. Nigeria has the largest economy in Africa, with a GDP of over $440 billion. | Key Concept: Nigeria's industrial structure has changed significantly. The economy has shifted from a primary-sector-dominated economy to one with a growing secondary and tertiary sector. However, it remains heavily dependent on oil. | Definition: Transnational Corporations (TNCs) are companies that operate in more than one country. They play a major role in Nigeria's economy, particularly in the oil and telecommunications sectors. | Limitations of Aid in Nigeria: Aid effectiveness is reduced by corruption -

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how Nigeria's industrial structure has changed since the 1960s. | Explain the role of TNCs in Nigeria's economic development. Use the example of Shell. | Assess the environmental impacts of economic development in Nigeria.

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Key Facts, Key Concept, Limitations of Aid in Nigeria, and one past-paper question.
